sections.h2: Where to record a deed for Adams County land
sections.html:
Deeds and mortgages for Adams County property go to the county recorder in West Union, at 110 West Main Street, Room 133, West Union, OH 45693. The county's recorder page prints two phone lines, 937-544-5051 and 937-544-2513. The counter is open Monday to Friday and closes at 4 in the afternoon.

Records can also be searched through the Adams County public access portal. The portal asks for a username and password, so create an account before you try a search. It also offers a real estate transfer alert service that flags new filings on a parcel, which owners use to catch fraud early.

If you are selling, you will usually not walk the deed in yourself. A closing agent or title company carries it between the auditor and the recorder. It still helps to know the route, so you can ask the right questions and check the charges on your settlement statement.

sections.h2: Recording fees set by Ohio law
sections.html:
Ohio sets recording fees by statute, so the Adams County counter cannot negotiate them. Section 317.32 of the Revised Code splits each charge into a base fee and a housing trust fund fee of the same size. On an ordinary instrument, pages one and two cost $17 plus $17 together, and each sheet after that (legal size, or any fraction of one, with the caption page counted) costs $4 plus $4.

The section also allows a document preservation surcharge of up to $5 per instrument, paid into the county general fund. Because the statute sets only a ceiling, ask the recorder which figure Adams County applies before you write the check.

Fees are collected at the counter when you hand the paper in. Electronic filers may settle afterward by electronic funds transfer, automated clearing house or a similar method. Ask the recorder how many pages your deed runs, since each page past the second adds to the fee.

In Ohio the deed stops at the county auditor before it reaches the recorder. Under section 319.202, whoever is taking title (or that person's representative) files a statement of value, either electronically or as three paper copies. The auditor endorses the deed with the fee charged and a note that the filing was made. The deed then goes to the recorder's window.

The seller pays up to two charges to the auditor at that stage:

  • The state-authorized conveyance fee in section 319.54(G)(3), which comes to $1 or ten cents for each hundred dollars of value (counting a partial hundred as a full one), whichever is larger.
  • A county real property transfer tax, but only where the commissioners have adopted one under section 322.02, limited to thirty cents on each hundred dollars and charged to the grantor.

Phone the auditor at 937-544-2364 to learn whether Adams County levies the optional tax. Other county numbers you may need: the treasurer at 937-544-2317, the commissioners at 937-544-3286 and the clerk of courts title department at 937-544-2345.

sections.h2: Transfers that skip the conveyance fee
sections.html:
Several family and court transfers are carved out of the auditor's fee in section 319.54(G)(3). The ones a seller or heir meets most often:

  • A gift between spouses, or from a parent to a child or to the child's spouse.
  • A deed whose only job is to fix or confirm one already on record.
  • A transfer made only to pledge property for a debt or to lift that pledge.
  • Property passing among the heirs or devisees of the same decedent with no money paid for it.
  • A deed into a trust whose maker kept an unlimited power to revoke it.
  • A transaction with no money or other valuable consideration that also is not a gift.
  • An interest valued at $100 or less.

When an exemption applies, the filing has to state the reason for it. Recording fees at the recorder's counter still apply to an exempt deed.

sections.h2: What the statement of value says about tax reductions
sections.html:
Section 319.202 ties the deed filing to the property tax bill. The buyer's statement either affirms that the seller said the preceding or current year's taxes will not be reduced under section 323.152, or it comes with a sworn instrument giving the estimated reduction. If the property has farm-use valuation, a similar affirmation covers the current agricultural use value and any recoupment charge.

Before closing, find out which reductions your parcel carries. The auditor's office can tell you, and the same 937-544-2364 number answers CAUV farm valuation questions.

sections.h2: A quick sale or an inherited house
sections.html:
A sale to a cash buyer follows the usual route: a deed, a statement of value at the auditor, then recording at the West Union counter. A closing agent or title company usually carries the paperwork between those two offices. If you handle it without an agent, ask the auditor about the conveyance fee and any optional county tax first, then ask the recorder for the page rate and surcharge.

Inherited houses add steps, because the person signing must have authority over the estate. Heirs should check with the court that handles the estate before signing a deed, and ask the title agent what proof the recorder will want attached.

A short checklist before you sign:

  • Call the auditor to confirm the conveyance fee and whether a county transfer tax applies.
  • Call the recorder for the page count rate and the surcharge.
  • Ask whether your transfer fits one of the exempt categories, and have the reason ready to state on the filing.
  • Confirm whether the property has farm-use valuation or a tax reduction on the parcel.

Adams County, with West Union as its seat and largest village, had an estimated 27,865 residents in July 2025 and 12,808 housing units. The owner-occupancy rate is 71.7 percent for 2020 to 2024, the median value of an owner-occupied home is $164,200, and median gross rent is $732 a month. Median household income is $50,264.

Those are county-wide figures, so a river-view lot and a village house can price very differently. Use recent sales near your parcel to set an asking price.

faqs.q: How do I reach the Adams County recorder by phone?
faqs.a: Call 937-544-5051 or 937-544-2513, the two lines on the recorder's page. The counter is open weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. at 110 West Main Street, Room 133, in West Union.

faqs.q: What will the Adams County recorder charge to file a deed?
faqs.a: Ohio Revised Code 317.32 sets $17 plus a matching $17 housing trust fund fee for pages one and two, then $4 plus $4 per added page. A county surcharge of up to $5 may sit on top, so get the final total from the recorder.

faqs.q: Is there a county transfer tax on an Adams County sale?
faqs.a: The statewide conveyance fee reaches most sales. An extra county tax exists only if the commissioners adopted one, so ask the auditor at 937-544-2364 whether Adams County did.

faqs.q: Which side files the statement of value on an Adams County sale?
faqs.a: The person taking title, or a representative, files it with the auditor, electronically or in three paper copies. The seller pays the conveyance fee and any county tax at that point.

faqs.q: Is a deed from parent to child exempt from the conveyance fee in Adams County?
faqs.a: Generally yes. Gifts from a parent to a child or the child's spouse appear on the exemption list in section 319.54(G)(3), but the filing must give the reason and recording fees still apply.
